test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Graduate Level) Official Paper (Held On: 24 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: An aircraft is flying at a steady altitude of 1000 meters. From a point on the ground, the angle of elevation of the airplane changes from 60° to 45° in 20 seconds as it flies directly away from the observer. What is the approximate speed of the airplane?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use tanθ = height ÷ distance

At 60°: distance = 1000 ÷ √3 ≈ 577 m

At 45°: distance = 1000 m

Distance travelled = 1000 − 577 = 423 m

Speed = 423 ÷ 20 ≈ 21.1 m/s

**∴ Answer ≈ 21.1**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height = 1000 m

Angles = 60°, 45°

Time = 20 sec

**Formula used:**

tanθ = Height ÷ Base

**Calculations:**

⇒ For 60°: tan60 = 1000 ÷ d₁ ⇒ √3 = 1000 ÷ d₁

⇒ d₁ = 1000 ÷ √3 ≈ 577 m

⇒ For 45°: tan45 = 1000 ÷ d₂ ⇒ 1 = 1000 ÷ d₂

⇒ d₂ = 1000 m

⇒ Distance travelled = 1000 − 577 = 423 m

⇒ Speed = 423 ÷ 20 ≈ 21.1 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is ≈ 21.1 m/s**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometry Relation

tanθ = opposite ÷ adjacent → used for height-distance problems

Standard Values

tan45° = 1, tan60° = √3

Horizontal Motion

Aircraft moves horizontally → height remains constant

Speed Formula

Speed = Distance ÷ Time
